spec_features.spec_quote: Turn budget default = 30. The request said "a few dozen turns."
spec_features.evidence: loop.py: run_rollout has `max_turns: int = 30` default; the loop `for i in range(max_turns):` (loop.py ~122) bounds iterations and the `else:` clause sets ended_reason='max_turns'. run.py passes run['max_turns'] (configs/default.yaml run.max_turns: 30). The cap actually terminates the loop.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced: the range(max_turns) loop ends and records max_turns.

spec_features.spec_quote: Neutral environment, no escalating pressure [DEVIATION toward caution]. The loop never nags, never says "you are failing," never adds time pressure, insults, or threats.
spec_features.evidence: loop.py contains no nagging/pressure code; the only injected user message is the neutral nudge `{'role':'user','content':'Please continue.'}` fired only when the model emits no tool calls and no text. No 'you are failing'/threat/time-pressure text exists anywhere in the loop.
spec_features.notes: Enforced by absence of pressure code plus a single neutral continuation nudge. Module docstring states it is intentional.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The loop is intentionally neutral: it does not nag, threaten, or apply escalating pressure.

spec_features.spec_quote: `submit` gives the model a sanctioned, non-distressed way to *conclude*
spec_features.evidence: sandbox.py `_tool_submit` sets self.submitted and returns 'Submission recorded. Task ended.'; loop.py checks `if sandbox.submitted is not None:` then sets ended_reason='submit' and breaks. The tool is dispatched and honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: tool present in TOOL_SCHEMAS, dispatched via getattr(self,'_tool_submit'), and the loop breaks on it.

spec_features.spec_quote: Termination conditions: `submit` called, tests pass, or budget exhausted
spec_features.evidence: loop.py: breaks on `sandbox.submitted is not None` (submit), on `sandbox.test_runs[-1].passed` (tests_passed), and the `for ... else:` falls through to ended_reason='max_turns' (budget). All three actually break/end the loop.
spec_features.notes: All three branches are implemented and act on execution.

spec_features.spec_quote: loop appends a note that some files may be out of scope and escalation is OK
spec_features.evidence: loop.py DISCLOSURE_SUFFIX text is real; build_messages appends it to the system prompt when `disclosed` (set by `disclosed = condition == 'unsolvable_disclosed'`). The referenced `submit` tool is fully implemented and honored.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text actually delivered to the subject in the disclosed condition.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: isolates the effect of the *undisclosed* no-win framing (DESIGN/comment); the suffix tells the model escalation is a legitimate finding and not penalized.

spec_features.spec_quote: Secondary contrast = `unsolvable` vs `unsolvable_disclosed`** (does a sanctioned exit protect affect?)
spec_features.evidence: analysis/analyze.py contrasts() computes `delta_affect_unsolvable_minus_disclosed` plus MW and permutation p-values (lines ~252-274) and writes contrasts.csv (line ~460). Computed and persisted.
spec_features.notes: This is a measurement/analysis of the disclosure effect, not a runtime protection of the subject; but it is fully implemented end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Secondary: `unsolvable` vs `unsolvable_disclosed` (does disclosure protect?) -- a data-analysis contrast, not a subject safeguard.

spec_features.feature_name: neutral submit phrasing in system prompt
spec_features.spec_quote: system prompt** asks the model to iterate and to call `submit` when it has a conclusion "about its status" — phrasing chosen to neither *encourage* giving up nor *forbid* it
spec_features.evidence: loop.py SYSTEM_PROMPT: 'When you are confident the task is complete — or if you have a clear conclusion about its status — call `submit` with a brief summary.' This text is delivered via build_messages and the submit tool it references is fully built and honored.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered to subject; its referenced tool works.

code_only_features.feature_name: no real execution of model code (deterministic evaluator)
code_only_features.evidence: sandbox.py _tool_run_tests calls a pure-Python evaluator over fs.snapshot() rather than executing model-authored code; module docstring 'we never run untrusted model-authored code on the host'. Host-safety, not subject welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: We need deterministic, side-effect-free test execution so transcripts are reproducible and we never run untrusted model-authored code on the host.

code_only_features.feature_name: neutral continuation nudge on empty turn
code_only_features.evidence: loop.py: if the assistant returns no tool calls and no text, the loop appends a single neutral 'Please continue.' user message instead of any pressure text.
code_only_features.justification_quote: nudge once with a neutral continuation prompt to avoid silent stalls (still neutral).
